original_card.question: Can the 64-per-call centre path (eight rank-8 COPY/ERASE totals through the private temporary) be shared across calls or shrunk?
methods: Derive a fully charged favorable relaxation for sharing one centre path across k calls, including restoration, hosting and precision.
Prove a lower bound on copied information per call for the selected decoder contract.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show the changed centre charge and copy profile per call with every added restoration or hosting cost charged, and its ceiling via ceiling.ceiling(centre=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the per-call centre charge and copy children for sharing across k = 2 calls, charge the sharing overhead, and screen it; stop this route if even the ideal sharing gains under 10%. Ideal budgets: free 2.80x, shared by two 1.90x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The centre path consumes 64 of about 99.6 unpaid coordinates per call, i.e. about 64% of the raw deficit.
allowed_variations: One sharing pattern across a fixed number of calls.
One reduced copied-total contract for the existing decoder.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Removing copies without a replacement contract for the decoder's copied totals.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: Lower bounds on the P104 centre (owned descent mass per FULL) for every word with the P104 mains and root-code centre contents, allowing multi-generation descents (contents built from earlier owned landings), which Model C does not price.
scope_change_reason: The P104 centre is 56 per FULL rather than the selected word's 64; the open lever is shrinking it by re-descending landed contents. A floor in that model answers whether the lever exists before any construction.
bottleneck_link: Each unit removed from the 56-unit P104 centre is worth about +7e-5 kappa on the P104 frontier invoice (0.81 units reach C = 0.0031). Single-generation decoder floors (Theorem 4 of ideal-decoder-floors, frontier-format Theorem P) do not cover multi-generation words.
stop_rule: Stop after the master inequality, the profiles it closes (R_8 = 8, R_8 = 7, and R_8 = 6 with R_7 = 8) with exact certificates, and a precise statement of the residual shallow covering problem; no construction search beyond the recorded screens.
evidence: PROOF.md; verify.py (common.py, floor.py) with controls; RESULT.json
author: G. V. Chudnovsky
ai_assistance: Substantial Anthropic Claude assistance (analysis, code and drafting) for G. V. Chudnovsky.

open_questions.question: Shallow covering problem: with Z = (V'_8)^perp of dim s and pairs (beta_j in Z, frame F_j of level <= 7) such that proj_Z(r_p) lies in span{beta_j : p in world(F_j)} for every port, is the number of pairs at least sum_i (9 - max(delta_i, 2))?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only gap between Theorems A-C and a complete root-code floor of 56 for the P104 centre; a counterexample whose contents are available would be a sub-56 centre (about +7e-5 kappa per unit).
open_questions.first_step: Decide s = 2 with delta = (7, 6): show four pairs (one on the line of Z_7 and three at level <= 6) cannot cover; a removed-root T is covered by three level-6 worlds, so the plane pair must be used.
open_questions.blocked_by: Coverage alone gives only s + 1 pairs (Singleton type); a plane-level analogue of Theorem 4 is needed for s >= 3.

open_questions.question: Does the floor extend to non-root-code centre contents (rank-9 realisations, contents outside the root code)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These are the open decoder cases (b)-(d) of decoder-floors-frontier-format, now in the multi-generation word model.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat Lemma 2 for general first-generation contents: they exist at every frame, so the feed inequality must charge them.
open_questions.blocked_by: The rank-per-level potential uses that root-code sources sit only at levels 0 and 1.

outcome_note: Any root-code P104 centre, multi-generation included, costs at least 56 unless at least two independent content directions never reach a line, with at least one of them ending above the planes if there are only two. The selected 56 meets the master inequality with equality; an explicit multi-generation centre also reaches 56 with R_8 = 8.
